title: Call a Rust command and read a file with the fs plugin

steps.task: Confirm the scaffold's `greet` command answers over IPC: invoking `greet` with the name "Tauri" returns the greeting string.
Add the tauri-plugin-fs dependency to the Rust backend and register the plugin with the app builder. The greet command must keep working.

mutations.diff:
--- a/src-tauri/Cargo.toml
+++ b/src-tauri/Cargo.toml
@@ -20,6 +20,7 @@
 [dependencies]
 tauri = { version = "2", features = [] }
 tauri-plugin-opener = "2"
+tauri-plugin-fs = "2"
 serde = { version = "1", features = ["derive"] }
 serde_json = "1"

--- a/src-tauri/src/lib.rs
+++ b/src-tauri/src/lib.rs
@@ -8,6 +8,7 @@
 pub fn run() {
     tauri::Builder::default()
         .plugin(tauri_plugin_opener::init())
+        .plugin(tauri_plugin_fs::init())
         .invoke_handler(tauri::generate_handler![greet])
         .run(tauri::generate_context!())
         .expect("error while running tauri application");

steps.task: Let the frontend read files from the app's data directory using the fs plugin. Reading must fail before the capability is granted and succeed after.
